source_snapshot.purpose_facts: Map every OCP slot to its Intel PCIe socket/port, inject `errType='uce'` under Windows through ITP/Cscripts, and verify the platform remains operational while recording platform-dependent BMC/uEFI/indicator behavior.
procedure_facts: Verify the platform recipe and establish a clean evidence boundary.
Deploy Intel ITP, boot Windows, start a full log and halt the target.
Capture `pcie.topology()` and `pcie.port_map()`, verify the OCP target, run `ei.injectPcieError(socket, port, errType='uce')`, then resume.
Collect results, photos and unexpected-event evidence.
criteria_facts: BMC may record a PCIe error.
uEFI SEL may record a PCIe error.
source_conflicts: The source boots Windows but lists Linux dmesg/syslog as generic post-test examples.

The test-set title requires an uncorrectable non-fatal result, while the shown generic `uce` call does not document which injected condition or platform severity policy guarantees non-fatal/recoverable handling.
missing_source_information: N and the complete OCP slot-to-device-BDF-to-root-port/socket/port map.
Exact device identity, link state, traffic state and supported recovery for each slot.
The precise UCE subtype/severity programming and expected Windows WHEA/CPER record.
Per-platform expected/optional BMC, uEFI and LED behavior.
Per-slot timeout, recovery and completion rules.

original_test_intent.statement: For every required OCP slot, inject the approved Intel PCIe uncorrectable non-fatal condition at the correctly mapped socket/port and verify recoverable handling, normal platform/device operation and the platform-specific records and indicator response.
must_preserve: OCP slots 1 through N, not one representative slot.
Uncorrectable non-fatal/recoverable PCIe behavior, not correctable or fatal injection.
Windows and the exact `pcie.topology()`, `pcie.port_map()` and `ei.injectPcieError(..., errType='uce')` flow.
BMC/uEFI/LED criteria as platform-conditional `may` behavior until a signed expectation defines them.
must_not_infer: That OCP slot numbering equals socket/port or BDF numbering.
That the generic string `uce` alone proves recoverable severity.
That every platform must produce BMC/uEFI records or assert a chassis LED.
That Linux AER/dmesg is valid evidence for this Windows run.

v2_review_conclusion.summary: V2 keeps the gated hybrid class, requires physical/logical slot mapping and recovery, and recognizes fatal escalation risk.
v2_review_conclusion.specific_gap: V2 uses Linux dmesg for a Windows run, does not require a device-BDF/root-port map or explicit per-slot iteration, and turns source-conditional BMC/uEFI behavior into broadly expected evidence without a platform policy.

related_records: Other rows reuse the title `OCP slot 1~N` for correctable, AMD and different PCIe fault types; none can supply this Intel non-fatal recipe.
applicable_history.precedence_application: Reliability row 33 alone defines this Intel uncorrectable non-fatal variant; same-title rows are explicitly excluded.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the gated hybrid class but require one signed OCP slot/BDF/root-port/socket/port tuple at a time, Windows-native proof that the injected record is recoverable/non-fatal, and an explicit platform expectation for each optional BMC/uEFI/LED observation.

conditions_present: The intended slot coverage, Windows/ITP location, topology commands, generic UCE call and conditional observations are known.
missing: Complete OCP matrix and N; precise UCE subtype/severity recipe; expected Windows record; per-device workload/recovery; platform-specific BMC/uEFI/LED policy; timeout, approvals and restoration.
provider: Platform owner supplies OCP physical/device/topology and expected-observation matrices.
Intel/ODM FAE supplies the signed injection and severity recipe.
Lab owner supplies a dedicated SUT, qualified observer, authorization and recovery window.
safe_read_only_work: Inventory each OCP device, serial, firmware, driver, BDF, link and root-port ancestry under Windows and OOB.
Capture `pcie.topology()` and `pcie.port_map()` only when the approved tool attachment is known non-mutating.
Export current Windows WHEA, BMC and uEFI records and photograph baseline indicators without clearing logs.
prohibited_until_resolved: BIOS changes, log clear, halt, fault injection, device reset, power cycle, failover, retry or final restoration.
closure_evidence: Signed per-slot matrix reconciles physical slot, device/serial/BDF, root port and ITP socket/port.
The recipe identifies the injected UCE condition and expected recoverable severity/record fields.
Optional-record/LED expectations, stop thresholds, recovery, authorization and final-state checks are signed.

revision_candidate.test_name: Intel OCP Slot 1~N PCIe Uncorrectable Non-Fatal Injection
revision_candidate.purpose: Inject the approved recoverable uncorrectable PCIe condition into every required OCP slot and verify correct target attribution, non-fatal handling, platform/device recovery and the exact platform-defined record and indicator behavior.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: Only the Intel server, BIOS/BMC/firmware, Windows build, OCP devices/drivers and ITP/Cscripts release covered by the signed platform and FAE recipes.
revision_candidate.target_scope: Every populated and explicitly required OCP slot 1~N in the signed matrix, one at a time. Each row must bind physical slot/label, device identity/serial/BDF, upstream root port and ITP socket/port. Exclude ordinary PCIe slots and all correctable, fatal, AMD, LCRC, ECRC, ACS and poisoned-TLP variants. Treat 15/10 minutes as estimates.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: N and signed OCP slot/device/BDF/root-port/socket/port matrix; device idle/test-traffic and recovery policy; exact UCE subtype and severity programming; approved ITP/Cscripts build/hash/API; six BIOS values and restore plan; Windows WHEA/CPER expected severity and identifiers; per-slot BMC/uEFI/LED expectation matrix; evidence window, timeout, go/no-go, authorization and recovery.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Retain and hash Windows/BMC/uEFI baselines before any approved clear or establish an approved timestamp marker. Apply the six BIOS settings through a qualified operator and boot the supported Windows image. Reconcile `pcie.topology()` and `pcie.port_map()` with the signed physical/BDF matrix. For each approved slot, create a unique full log, confirm the device state and exact socket/port, halt, run one exact `ei.injectPcieError(socket, port, errType='uce')` invocation under the signed non-fatal recipe, resume immediately, and collect Windows-native severity/identity, conditional OOB/firmware/LED and device-health evidence before the next go/no-go. Restore all settings after the matrix.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Exact OCP matrix and non-fatal recipe approved; platform and package verified; dedicated idle or recipe-defined traffic SUT; no production dependency; baselines retained; clocks/storage synchronized; physical observer and console/OOB/recovery proven; all BIOS, log-clear, ITP, halt/injection/resume, device-recovery, reset and restoration approvals recorded.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Platform/tool identity and hashes; signed per-slot map; device firmware/driver/BDF/link and before/after function; BIOS before/during/after; baseline/clear audit; full topology/port-map output; per-slot exact injection and halt/resume log; Windows WHEA/CPER evidence decoded as recoverable/non-fatal and tied to the target PCIe identity; BMC/uEFI records and front-panel state according to the signed expectation matrix; anomalies, recovery, final inventory/link/function and restored-state proof.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: The signed Intel/ODM non-fatal UCE recipe and platform OCP expectation matrix. UEFI CPER defines recoverable as non-fatal uncorrected; the source additionally requires normal system operation. Source `may` observations are accepted only against the signed per-platform expected/optional matrix, not as universal requirements or dispensable evidence.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Critical PCIe fault injection on a dedicated SUT only. Do not guess slot/port/BDF mapping, infer severity from `uce`, inject a production or management-critical device, reuse another OCP/PCIe pattern, substitute Linux logs, expose secrets, filter evidence, leave the target halted, auto-loop, retry, or continue after wrong target/severity, fatal escalation, device loss, unexpected LED/state or instability.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Platform owner approves the per-slot matrix and device impact; FAE approves the exact UCE subtype/severity, tool and target; qualified operator changes BIOS and observes physical indicators. Each slot's halt/injection/resume, next-slot go/no-go, recovery and final restoration require signed authorization.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Operator/FAE owns BIOS changes, physical slot/indicator confirmation and exceptional device/platform recovery. An authorized Agent may run the exact bounded Cscript injection and collect/correlate Windows, OOB, firmware and device evidence after the matrix and recipe are signed; engineering decides final disposition.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On wrong target, fatal severity, failure to resume, device disappearance/link loss, crash/no-boot, persistent AER/WHEA state or unexpected indicator, stop the matrix, preserve unfiltered evidence and use only the per-device/platform approved recovery. Restore BIOS/tool state and prove final device/link/system health before any separately approved rerun.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Unresolved slot/BDF/socket/port or non-fatal severity mapping; mismatched device/tool/BIOS; missing baseline, observer, approval, evidence or recovery; topology disagreement; halt/resume failure; wrong target; fatal or unspecified severity; unexpected reset/hang, device/function/link loss, error storm or thermal/power instability; any mismatch against the signed BMC/uEFI/LED expectation; or failed recovery/restoration/final health.

identified_defects: V2 does not make the 1~N per-slot matrix and per-slot go/no-go explicit.
V2 treats generic `uce` as sufficient for the non-fatal intent without requiring recoverable severity proof.
V2 adds Linux dmesg evidence to an explicit Windows procedure.
V2 does not preserve the source's conditional `may` semantics for BMC/uEFI/LED behavior as a platform-specific expectation matrix.
reason_for_change: Prevent wrong-slot, wrong-severity and wrong-OS evidence while preserving complete OCP 1~N coverage and platform-specific optional observations.

new_technical_evidence.title: UEFI Specification 2.11, Appendix N: Common Platform Error Record
new_technical_evidence.applicability: CPER severity and PCIe error records used by WHEA-capable platforms
new_technical_evidence.supports: CPER severity 0 is Recoverable, also called non-fatal uncorrected; PCIe sections carry device and AER information used to verify severity and target identity.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: The platform recipe must define which fields and UCE subtype this injection should produce.

new_technical_evidence.title: Hardware Errors and Error Sources
new_technical_evidence.supports: Windows distinguishes nonfatal uncorrected errors as conditions for which the OS can attempt recovery and identifies PCIe root-port reporting as an error source.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: Exact event channel, identifiers and recovery expected for each OCP device remain platform-specific.

new_technical_evidence.title: Source testcase Wistron-System RAS-00753-V003
new_technical_evidence.applicability: Only the Intel OCP uncorrectable non-fatal row
new_technical_evidence.supports: The source fixes OCP 1~N, Windows, topology/port-map commands, generic UCE injection and conditional BMC/uEFI/LED criteria.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: N, mapping, UCE subtype, severity proof and platform expectations are absent.

removed_ambiguities: Binds every physical OCP slot to device/BDF/root-port and ITP targeting identifiers.
Requires recoverable/non-fatal severity evidence rather than inferring it from `uce`.
Turns each source `may` observation into a signed platform expectation instead of a universal assumption.
Excludes same-title Intel correctable and AMD/other PCIe variants and Linux evidence.
resolved_blockers: The missing package, map and severity recipe are provider-closable, so the capability remains REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.
remaining_blockers: Execution awaits the exact OCP matrix, approved UCE subtype/severity and package, Windows record expectations, per-platform optional behavior, authorization and recovery.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 makes 1~N auditable per slot, proves non-fatal severity and target identity in Windows, and avoids both over-requiring and silently ignoring platform-conditional BMC/uEFI/LED behavior.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Contract-only validation recovered every signed OCP matrix row, exact physical/BDF/root-port/ITP mapping, independent non-fatal severity proof, per-slot approval and recovery, and platform-defined conditional evidence. It rejected representative coverage, severity inference from `uce`, API-only completion and automatic iteration/retry.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: Reliability row 33 maps OCP slots 1~N with Intel topology/port commands, injects generic UCE under Windows and expects normal operation with conditional BMC/uEFI/LED observations.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 retains the correct class and general risk but lacks per-slot BDF mapping, severity proof and conditional-evidence policy, and uses Linux logs.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow read-only inventory and baseline export; prohibit BIOS, clear, halt/injection and recovery until every slot and severity rule is signed.
